facts.statement: Futabasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically in the Santonian age.
Futabasaurus is a genus of plesiosaur found in the Late Cretaceous deposits of Fukushima, Japan.
facts.quote: Futabasaurus is a genus of plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Fukushima, Japan.

facts.statement: The genus Futabasaurus was formally described and named in 2006.
facts.quote: It was described and named in 2006

facts.statement: Futabasaurus is classified within the family Elasmosauridae.
facts.quote: and was assigned to the family Elasmosauridae.

facts.statement: Futabasaurus holds the distinction of being the first elasmosaurid discovered in Japan.
facts.quote: Futabasaurus is the first elasmosaurid found in Japan.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Futabasaurus was discovered in the Irimazawa Member of the Tamayama Formation within the Futaba Group in Fukushima Prefecture.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Futabasaurus was found in the Irimazawa Member of the Tamayama Formation, in the Futaba Group of Fukushima Prefecture, Japan.

facts.statement: The fossils of Futabasaurus were discovered by Tadashi Suzuki, who was a high school student at the time.
facts.quote: The fossils were found by Tadashi Suzuki, then a high school student.

facts.statement: Many bones of the Futabasaurus type specimen show evidence of predation or scavenging by the shark Cretalamna.
facts.quote: Many of the bones of the type specimen show signs of apparent scavenging or predation by sharks, specifically Cretalamna.

facts.statement: The genus name Futabasaurus honors the Futaba Group where it was found, while the species name suzukii honors the discoverer's family name, Suzuki.
facts.quote: The genus Futabasaurus was named after the Futaba Group, in which it was discovered; the specific name is derived from the family name of its discoverer, Suzuki.

facts.statement: Futabasaurus is estimated to have been over 6 meters long, with a possible range between 6.4 and 9.2 meters.
facts.quote: Futabasaurus has been estimated over 6 m in length, possibly within the range of 6.4 - 9.2 m.

facts.statement: Futabasaurus is distinguished from other elasmosaurids by a long distance between eye sockets and nostrils, fused interclavicles and clavicles, a relatively long humerus, and slim femora with prominent muscle scars.
facts.quote: It can be distinguished from other elasmosaurids by the following characteristics: there is a long distance between the eye sockets and nostrils; the interclavicles and clavicles are fused, and the anterior edge is bent; the humerus is relatively long; and the femora are slim and show prominent muscle scars.

facts.statement: Futabasaurus lived between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Futabasaurus was approximately 7 meters long and weighed between 3 and 4 tonnes.
facts.quote: La longitud era de cerca de 7 metros, y pesaba entre 3 a 4 toneladas.

facts.statement: Futabasaurus possessed a long distance between its eye sockets and nostrils.
facts.quote: Una larga distancia entre las cuencas oculares y las fosas nasales.

facts.statement: The clavicles and interclavicles of Futabasaurus were fused, with a curved anterior edge.
facts.quote: Las clavículas e interclavículas están fusionadas y el borde anterior está curvado.

facts.statement: Futabasaurus had a relatively long humerus.
The femur of Futabasaurus was very thin and featured significant muscle impressions.
facts.quote: Un fémur muy delgado con una impresión muscular significativa.

facts.statement: The name Futabasaurus was also applied to an unnamed theropod dinosaur from Japan, which remains a nomen nudum and is distinct from the plesiosaur.
facts.quote: The name "Futabasaurus" has also been used for an unrelated theropod dinosaur, from the Late Cretaceous Ashizawa Formation of Japan. However, this dinosaur was not officially named, and remains a nomen nudum.
